findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. The next two paragraphs say what a study is and why this one exists.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: Someone arriving at the Athena site gets one paragraph about Athena and then a long technical reading of a different project, firstmate. The ledes explain why, but a reader who came to learn about Athena may not see that the rest of the page is meant as a demonstration.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the lede "This page is that study of firstmate."

findings.text: What to do next is clear and concrete: prerequisites, clone, setup, and a first command, linked from the top of the page. One gap: the word "predictions" in "It shows how it read the request and its predictions" is never explained.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link speaks to the site's owner, not to a newcomer. Placed in the header, it may make a first-time reader think there is something they are supposed to decide.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The firstmate study starts well. It gives a one-sentence definition, defines terms before they are used, and walks one task from start to finish, so a newcomer can follow the main path without the transition cards.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker"

findings.text: The transition cards are dense and full of qualifiers. A newcomer will find them heavy going. They read more like a reference for experts than an explanation.
findings.source: Transitions, card t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; a local-only project also counts..."

findings.text: Several definitions appear twice with the same wording, and the page says so: "Each is defined here, and again in the Glossary". This makes an already long page longer without adding anything.
findings.source: "Words used first" entries for "in scope" and "red", repeated word for word in the Glossary

findings.text: Being open about what the study did not run builds trust. However, the note about an earlier reading that missed paths describes how the study was made, which a newcomer neither needs nor can act on.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths..."

findings.text: This sentence is awkward and its meaning is unclear; it seems to mean the definitions that follow. It is a small slip in an otherwise carefully worded page.
findings.source: Transitions lead-in: "The two deciders are explained below the cards' heading."
